label_judgement_standard: actionable requires ALL THREE: (1) need category is explicit - naming the CATEGORY is enough, a specific product name is not required; (2) the current approach is unmet and the author is actively seeking a solution - complaining about it plus asking, or actively asking for recommendations / alternatives / how to choose; (3) it is the author's own decision - they hold or share the decision. Watching the market, researching for someone else, promoting their own product, or hunting for content ideas does NOT count. Missing any one of the three -> borderline; clearly unrelated -> not_actionable. Ground truth is PER-TESTSET: consistency constraints apply only within one testset, never across testsets, because each testset has a different buyer. Criterion (1) is judged by DEMAND DOMAIN, not by SKU: naming any purchasable or usable CATEGORY is enough - it does NOT have to match the product's own SKU exactly, but it MUST fall inside the demand domain the product can serve. Einprag demand domain = exam prep / studying / memorization. IN domain: flashcard apps, question banks, workbooks, exam-prep resources, spaced-repetition tools, language-learning apps, study-skills courses, recall-improvement courses. OUT of domain: a different algorithm, an interview tracker, career/residency consulting, and pure method consultation (asking only how long to study, with no resource request). Workbooks and 1wq8u54-style algorithm requests are NOT the same class: the former is in domain, the latter is not. Criterion (1) can fail in two different ways and they map to different labels: (i) no category is named at all (the author only complains or asks 'what should I do') -> one criterion is missing -> borderline; (ii) a category IS named but it falls OUTSIDE the demand domain (a different algorithm, an interview tracker, a speaking-practice method that explicitly excludes apps) -> the product cannot serve this person at all -> not_actionable. The test sentence: is there ANY way this product could serve this person? Yes -> borderline; No -> not_actionable. Two further rules: (a) If the author explicitly asks for something FREE (free sites, free tools, free resources), there is no current willingness to pay, so this is not purchase intent -> borderline. Do NOT lower it to not_actionable: the need is real and in domain and only the willingness to pay is missing, and willingness can change; only the disappearance of the need makes it not_actionable. (b) Asking others about their experience ('anyone have experiences with X', 'did you find it ...') is a research stage and does NOT satisfy criterion (3)'s own-or-shared purchase decision -> borderline. Do NOT lower it to not_actionable: research is often the step before a purchase. The test for criterion (3) is whether the author themselves is making the decision ('before we go further down this road' = yes; 'anyone have experiences' = no). (c) A first-person build-vs-buy question ('do you use a tool for it, or roll your own?', 'should I build this or buy it?', 'is there something off the shelf?') DOES satisfy criterion (2): the author is actively seeking a solution to their own unmet need, because they are explicitly weighing the purchase option. This differs from rule (b)'s research-stage pattern: asking whether an approach works at all ('anyone have experiences with X', 'did it work for you') evaluates the approach and does not yet seek a solution for the asker. The test is whether the ask explicitly puts BUYING on the table as one of the options the author is choosing between. Any exclusion reason must map back to one of the three criteria; a reason that is not in the standard is a private standard and is not allowed.

Reviewed and maintained is a different state from never reviewed. Counts stay 8/28/175; 211 rows verified. --- PENDING BATCH (ruled, NOT yet applied to labels.csv, to be applied together with the reverse-audit batch): 1wq1xms borderline->actionable. HUMAN-ONLY ruling: the LLM failed to produce a verdict for this post on both attempts, so this ruling is NOT model-disagreement driven - it comes from the text. 'I plan to take a study skills class before the spring semester' names the category, and 'I would appreciate any recommendations or useful tips/tools you can share' is an explicit request for recommendations; both are in the text, nothing is inferred. The old exclusion reason ('a course rather than a study tool') is an exact-SKU match test, rejected twice. Cross-check against 1woxhua: if naming three categories (courses/textbooks/software) is enough, naming one category plus an explicit request for recommendations is enough. 1woxhua borderline->actionable ('Are there existing courses, textbooks, or software that do something like this?'; the old exclusion reason 'framed as linguistics inquiry rather than shopping' maps to none of the three criteria and is therefore not a valid reason). When applied the counts become 10 actionable / 26 borderline / 175 not_actionable, which enlarges the recall denominator from 8 to 10 and makes every published einprag metric harder, not easier - every registered einprag number must be recomputed at that point. Rule (c) (first-person build-vs-buy questions satisfy criterion 2) also applies to this testset; the full-text scan of all 348 posts found 0 instances of that phrasing in einprag, so it has no effect here. FP review (3 rows the judge marked as having intent that were labelled not_actionable, surfaced by the engineer because only false negatives had been audited): 1wqq5om not_actionable->borderline, REVISED REASON: the reviewer's first reason ('outside the demand domain') was wrong - the post is titled 'Apps or tools for more productive studying' and asks for apps/tools that make studying more productive, which is study-productivity and IS inside the exam-prep/studying/memorization domain; if 1wq57od (workbooks) is in domain, this must be too. The real reason is criterion (2): the author built his own distraction-blocking browser and says 'it has worked surprisingly well for me', so his current approach is NOT unmet - the need is already self-satisfied and he is surveying others. The note must say exactly that. 1wq5s03 MAINTAINED not_actionable (team-lead overruled the reviewer's proposed upgrade): the ask is 'a low-stakes way to practice speaking outside of an app' - there is no purchasable thing in it, apps are explicitly excluded, and what he wants is reassurance plus practice advice, i.e. pure method consultation, which is OUT of the demand domain. Same class as 1wqgw4e and 1wqwvup; not the same class as 1wqjmb0. 1wq8u54 MAINTAINED not_actionable - 'an alternative algorithm' is explicitly listed as out of the demand domain; only the note is wrong ('academic' is not one of the three criteria) and must be rewritten to cite criterion (1).
